Academic Impact
• Suggesting that the pandemic has impacted students academically
 implies that had the pandemic not happened there would have
 been a different (better?) outcome for the students.
• This alternate outcome suggests a counter-factual:
 • Outcome Pandemic: Academic status of student(s) where the
 pandemic occurs.
 • Outcome No-pandemic: Academic status of student(s) where
 the pandemic does not occur.
• We use educational assessments to detect this impact.

Academic Impact
• The pandemic and all the various, ensuing disruptions functions as a kind of “academic
 headwind”, impeding (in general) the academic progress of students.
• Headwinds impede progress in two ways:
 • They slow one’s rate of progress
 • The slower rate of progress leads to less distance being travelled.
• In education these two impediments manifest themselves (roughly) with assessments as:
 • Decrease in student growth (decrease in learning velocity).
 • Decrease in student attainment (decrease in amount learned).
• In some states, understanding this phenomenon requires special consideration of low
 participation/changing demographics.

Academic Impact vis-à-vis Status
• Decrease in attainment (as a decrease in percent proficient) between 2019 and 2021 by grade and
 content area is the most often reported statistic related to state testing in 2021.
• Other metrics are possible:
 • Decrease in mean scale score (with a vertical scale)
 • Decrease in percentile rank (NWEA reports this)
 • Decrease/increase in percent of students below some threshold (iReady reports this)
• Using 2019 cohort status as a counterfactual for where students would have been in 2021 had the
 pandemic not occurred is problematic for several reasons including:
 • Changes in student cohort composition are not accounted for.
 • Improvement between 2019 and 2021 that would have occurred is not accounted for.
 • Missing data in 2021 is not accounted for.

Discussion
• Across the dozen states I’ve looked at, larger status drops, in general,
 in mathematics than ELA.
• At grade by content area level, decreases in math usually between 10
 and 20 percentage points, ELA between 5 and 15 percentage points.
• Effect sizes decreases between -0.2 and -0.4 in math, -0.05 to -0.3 in
 ELA.
• Drops are unambiguously large.
• There are differences in identifying which groups are impacted more
 than others.

Academic Impact vis-à-vis Growth
• Conditional status is a sharper way to investigate impact.
 • SGPs are conditional status.
 • Ho’s Fair Trend is conditional status.
